2026-08-27: Root cause of the prior draft's 77-differing-halfword score was a mismodeled call, exactly the class already found on sibling owners this session. `Func_08007310` is not a real function: 0x08007310 is the fp (r11) slot of the fourteen-entry `_call_via_rN` trampoline bundle at games/gs1/asm/080072e4.s (`bx rN; mov r8,r8`, 4 bytes/slot, r0..sp). fp is never a valid argument-passing register on this compiler (arm_function_arg in alchemy-gcc/agscc/gcc/config/arm/arm.c stops argument passing at r3), so a 2-argument call to a symbol named 'Func_08007310' can never legitimately compile to code that also loads a call target into fp. Traced the true call target directly from games/gs1/asm/080c0cec.s using PC-relative literal-pool arithmetic (effective_addr = align4(instr_offset+4)+imm): the `ldr r2,[pc,#192]` at byte offset 58 resolves to pool slot 252, i.e. 0x0300013c, which is then moved into fp via `mov fp,r2` at offset 76 and never rewritten again before EITHER `bl Func_08007310` (offsets 84 and 212) -- both calls go through the exact same fp value, 0x0300013c, for the whole function.

0x0300013c is not a novel address: it is already an established, adopted helper in this exact codebase (grep confirms 4 independent recon/src files already call it this way), consistently modeled as a 2-argument function pointer cast/call with the literal address used directly as the callee, e.g. games/gs1/src/unidentified/main/battle/battle_owner_66.c's `typedef s32 (*ArmRatio)(s32,s32); ArmRatio ratio=(ArmRatio)0x0300013c; result=ratio(arg0,0x10000);` (with an explicit comment: '0x0300013c is the relocated ARM ratio helper... TWO arguments'), and games/gs1/recon/en/main/080f4028.c / games/gs1/src/camera/scene/configure.c's `((u32(*)(u32,u32))0x0300013c)(N, 192<<8)` -- note the second argument in those two siblings is literally `192<<8` = 0xc000, the exact same second argument this owner's disassembly requires (0xc000) at both call sites, strongly corroborating this is the identical helper with the identical calling convention. Rewrote both call sites as genuine indirect calls through this traced literal, `((u32(*)(u32,u32))0x0300013c)(arg0, 0xc000)`, removing the fictional Func_08007310 prototype/call entirely and matching object dump confirms both now compile through `_call_via_rN` veneers rather than a direct symbolic `bl`.

2026-08-27, residual after the fix: differing_halfwords regressed from 77 to 103 and candidate size grew from the correct 264 to 276 (12 bytes over). This is a real, measured regression versus the (semantically impossible) prior draft, but the prior draft's call-target shape can never reach exact regardless of tuning, since no valid N-argument call to a real function can ever legitimately load its target into fp on this compiler -- so it was a dead end. Root-caused the regression precisely via the compiler's own retained .insns/.s output (candidate-show --asm and the scratch/candidate-show/080c0cec/080c0cec.s intermediate): the compiler places the traced pointer in r2 at each call site (`bl _call_via_r2`, reloaded fresh via `ldr r2,[pc,#N]` at both sites) rather than fp, unlike the reference. Simultaneously, the second argument constant 0xc000 (which the reference recomputes fresh with `movs r1,#192; lsls r1,r1,#8` at BOTH call sites, per the retained asm) gets hoisted by this compiler's CSE into a single register (r7) held live across the whole function, which is exactly what displaces `scale` out of r7 (where the reference keeps it, used directly in ALU ops with zero overhead) into fp instead -- and since fp is a Thumb high register, every later arithmetic use of `scale` now costs an extra `mov r_lo,fp` pair the reference never needs (visible directly in the aligned diff as a 7-instruction block computing `scale*0x1fe` from fp instead of the reference's 3-instruction block using r7 directly). This fp/r7/r2 role reassignment is the entire source of the 12 extra bytes.
